corrections.correction: Do not present 5500–5000 BCE as the earliest secure Cuban occupation established by this batch. Old charcoal is not directly dated human remains and its association is problematic.
2754–2478 BCE falls after 5000 cal BP. The sample cannot support the export’s claim of pre-5000-cal-BP Cuban occupation.

corrections.input: A/B Playa del Mango cemetery span
corrections.correction: M2 cemetery: 116 BCE–241 CE; M2 domestic area: 55 BCE–435 CE; isolated M1 tooth: 125–435 CE. None establishes uninterrupted cemetery use until 435 CE.
The reported combined ca. 350 BCE–630 CE assemblages are not Late Pleistocene, and the combined range is not independently dated for each of the three sites.

Peros 2006 gives before 1220 CE to 1640 CE or later, with >40 collapsed structures. Cooper/Rojas 2004 separately cites >50 stilted houses. Preserve source-specific counts without treating either as a resident census.
The Middle Cauca Valley paper concerns Colombia and cannot directly establish Cuban settlement or a Yucatán–Cuba route.
C-1426 is Curaçao; defer its site record to the ABC-islands intake. Its age does not directly date Cuba.
Official Oxford publication date is 2017; export 2016 is not used as the book issue year.
PNAS paper was online 2024, issue 2025. Colten/Worthington was online 2018, issue 2019. Record both date contexts accurately.
Cultigen consumption does not itself locate fields; model isotope dietary ratios are not starch-grain count ratios. Archaeological tradition labels are not ethnic identities.
Roksandic 2015 and PNAS 2025 report different study-specific envelopes. Both are retained with provenance instead of silently selecting a consensus.
Mexico, Venezuela, Chile, Patagonia and Pampas references are logged as related, already covered or excluded from Cuban fact support.
